newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends higher on firm fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends higher on firm fundamentals.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures finished higher Thursday in tandem with a rally in western natural gas prices and further capacity reduction on the key Pacific Intertie, market sources said.
"You got a lot of reasons for this market to go higher," a Houston trader said.
November natural gas prices at the San Juan hub in New Mexico rose 10 cents per million British thermal units to the $1.87-$1.89 range, market sources said.
News of further transport reductions on the alternate current (AC) and direct current (DC) portions of the Intertie through mid-October bolstered futures and cash prices.
Bonneville Power Administration also raised most of its prices for power delivered to the Northwest on Friday.

Wednesday's outage of the 361 megawatt (MW) unit at the San Juan coal-fired generating station in New Mexico was also cited by some participants as a factor in today's rise. The San Juan unit 1, operated by Public Service of New Mexico, was was expected to resume operation Friday.
November California-Oregon Border (COB) futures finished up 63 cents at $18.23 a megawatt hour (MWh), the highest level since late August. The contract hit a session low of $17.90.
December COB ended up 45 cents at $19.25. Deferred COB settled flat to 34 cents higher.
November Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up 70 cents at $17.30 a MWh after being traded between $16.85 and $17.30.
December PV finished up 40 cents at $17.75. Active outer PV months ended flat to 60 cents higher.
Most participants expected the complex would extend today's gain Friday based on continued strength in the cash market in the western U.S.
NYMEX estimated 213 COB and 81 PV contracts were sold Thursday.
